subject: Hosted evaluation: endpoint mapping, rate caps, and quickstart next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Klein <sophie@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted evaluation: endpoint mapping, rate caps, and quickstart next steps

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear path for your Hosted evaluation:

Recap from our call:
- BrightCart is interested in validating the Hosted API for the conversational assistant in the checkout flow (PoC) before considering Dedicated capacity.
- Primary success criteria: <10% latency impact on checkout, consistent pass-through for moderation, and < 20% prediction cost overhead vs current heuristic approach.

Questions / info we need from your side to scope the quickstart:
1) Traffic shape: daily active users expected during PoC, expected peak concurrent requests and preferred go-live date for the trial.
2) Typical prompt size and expected average tokens per request (incl. system + user).
3) Any regulatory or network constraints that would push you toward Private (VPC) instead of Hosted.

Our initial Hosted configuration recommendations (for evaluation):
- Endpoints: use /v1/generate for completion payloads and /v1/chat for context-aware assistant. We'll map these to two separate rate classes so you can independently scale chat vs batch inference.
- Default ratecaps for evaluation tier: 120 requests/minute per endpoint, with burst up to 240r/min for short periods. Token throughput soft-limit: 200k tokens/minute by default for PoC; we can raise it temporarily for your demo window.
- Suggested test phasing: week 1 = smoke and integration tests (low qps), week 2 = scaled synthetic load to simulate peak, week 3 = limited beta with real users.

Attachments: I'm including an onboarding checklist and an endpoint/ratecap matrix that maps typical BrightCart flows to our Hosted rate classes. See attached: redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf and endpoint-ratecaps-matrix.csv

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the PoC start date window and expected peak qps/token profile (reply with numbers).
- We schedule a 30-minute quickstart session next week to wire up API keys, example payloads, and a short load test.
- If you need higher sustained throughput during evaluation, let us know and we can provision a temporary bump on the Hosted tier.

If Hosted looks good after the PoC we can map a path to Dedicated, but let's get the quick win first.

Thanks —
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Diego@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf (application/pdf, 48KB), endpoint-ratecaps-matrix.csv (text/csv, 6KB)
From: Sophie Klein <sophie@brightcart.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: endpoint mapping, rate caps, and quickstart next steps

Diego —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side so you can size the PoC:
- PoC audience: internal beta to ~1,000 shoppers/day initially, ramp to 10k/day by week 3 if performance looks good.
- Peak concurrency: expect up to ~30 concurrent assistant requests during checkout spikes (holiday test window we want to simulate).
- Tokens: average user + system prompt combined ~120 tokens, worst case ~450 tokens.
- Timeline: we'd like to start integration tests the week of July 12 and run the PoC July 19–30.
- Compliance: no on-prem constraint for PoC; we will need SOC2 evidence during procurement, but Hosted is acceptable for the trial. Procurement copied for contract discussions later.

Couple of questions: 
1) Can you confirm the Hosted burst behavior — you mentioned doubling request allowance briefly. Is that automatic or manual request to Redwood?
2) How do you recommend mapping our two main flows (checkout assistant + post-purchase insights batch job) to your endpoints and rate classes? The batch job will use larger context windows but is run off-peak.
3) Any simple cost estimate for the trial period using the numbers above? Even a ballpark helps our finance partner.

Sophie Klein
Head of Product, BrightCart
Sophie@brightcart.com | +1 (617) 555-4621
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Klein <sophie@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: endpoint mapping, rate caps, and quickstart next steps

Sophie —

Appreciate the details — this is perfect. Quick answers inline and a proposed plan: 

1) Burst behavior: we provide an automatic burst window for Hosted evals (short-lived, up to 2x configured r/minute for 5–10 minutes). For sustained increases we raise the soft limits for the trial window; that requires a quick internal change but no contract amendment. I'll flag Karthik to provision a temporary increase for your July 19–30 window if you confirm.

2) Endpoint mapping recommendation:
- Checkout assistant (low-latency, small context): map to /v1/chat, evaluation rate class = "interactive" (default 120 r/minute, burst to 240). This is optimized for short-turn, low-latency responses.
- Post-purchase insights batch job (large context, off-peak): map to /v1/generate, evaluation rate class = "batch" (configured by job; start at 30 r/minute with higher token throughput allowances). We can also use our asynchronous job endpoint to avoid tying up interactive capacity.

3) Ballpark cost: based on your numbers (10k/day average, ~120 tokens/request) the PoC token volume is approximately 1.2M tokens/day. For the Hosted eval rate tier a conservative estimate is ~$0.0006 per token (this is a trial/estimate only) → ~ $720/day. We will provide a formal pricing estimate with usage tiers once you confirm the PoC dates and sample payloads.

Next actions I can take right away:
- Karthik will provision a temporary trial ratecap bump for July 19–30 after you confirm the PoC window (no contract change needed).
- I'll schedule a 30-minute quickstart call for the week of July 12 (suggested slots: Jul 13 10:00-10:30 PDT or Jul 14 14:00-14:30 PDT). Please reply with preferred slot.
- Attachments: updated endpoint-ratecaps-matrix.csv includes the mapping I described; redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf lists API key steps, sample payloads, and a short load-test script.

If procurement needs SOC2 artifacts now, Marissa (cc'd) will share our SOC2 package and a short evidence ledger.

Look forward to getting this running — let me know the slot and I'll send the invite.

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Diego@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
